result.summary: Reviewed git diff main...HEAD, lib/letflow/design/req052-instance-cancellation.md, and Letflow.Engine.cancel_instance/3 against the four REVIEWER questions. (1) Idiomatic vs. crutch: cancel_instance/3 is a plain function using one Ecto.Multi (M1-M7), matching create/2's and complete_task/3's established pre-transaction-with-chain / single-Multi shape verbatim -- no gen_statem-simulating case/if, no manual process management. terminal?/1, Task.complete_changeset/2, and TokenRecord.advance_changeset/2 are reused unchanged rather than re-derived. (2) Supervision: verified lib/letflow/application.ex's diff removes only the Letflow.ApprovalSupervisor children entry, leaving Letflow.InstanceSupervisor (still supervising future REQ-056/057 consumers) untouched -- no orphaned child spec, no dangling process. Grepped lib/ and test/ for ApprovalSupervisor/ParallelApproval: only remaining hits are prose/historical cross-references (lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex's updated comparison sentence, lib/letflow/row_approval.ex's and lib/letflow/row_approval/approval.ex's 'what we deliberately chose not to do' commentary, engine.ex's own moduledoc/doc citing the SUPERSESSION) -- none reference a load-bearing call into a deleted module. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean. (3) Type-safety: cancel_error()'s tagged-tuple taxonomy is exhaustive and no new class of invalid state is representable only via runtime/property-test failure; no docs/issues/ entry filed. (4) Scope: no abstraction/behaviour/macro introduced ahead of REQ-052's own AC; cancel_instance/3 stays within the persistence-layer boundary create/2 and complete_task/3 already established, correctly declines to wire {:cancel_branch, _} through Transition (would only ever hit a defensive no-op given the undisputed join_counters persistence gap), and correctly declines to implement SCH-03 timer cancellation or REQ-056 HTTP-abort (named out-of-scope, S6/future-REQ-056 respectively). Decision 0006's :prefix mechanism is threaded through every Multi step and TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 call, consistent with every other Engine function. FLAGGED ITEM 1 (ApprovalSupervisor full deletion, diverging from REQ-046's InstanceSupervisor-retention precedent): SIGN-OFF. The design doc's §2 reasoning is sound and traceable, not asserted: InstanceSupervisor was retained specifically because stage-3-instance-engine.md names two distinct, still-open future consumers (REQ-056 service-task dispatch, REQ-057 plugin registry) for a supervised per-instance process; ApprovalSupervisor has no analogous named future consumer -- REQ-045 already settled 'no process, plain transactional context module' for the general running-instance shape, and REQ-051 explicitly frames ParallelApproval/ApprovalSupervisor as 'the hand-written special case of what PARALLEL_GATEWAY split/join now expresses as definition data.' Keeping a second idle DynamicSupervisor around on a symmetry argument alone would itself be the kind of speculative surface this project's anti-scope-creep stance warns against. This is a reasoned divergence, not a shortcut. FLAGGED ITEM 2 (OQ-2, join_counters never persisted so AC5 'agreement by construction' is asserted not mechanically enforced): ACCEPTABLE to ship as a documented open question, not a blocking scope gap. The 'agreement by construction' argument is logically sound as stated, not hand-waved: cancel_instance/3 is, by the design doc's own traced audit (§4), the only code path in the shipped codebase that ever persists instance_projections.status = :cancelled -- Transition's {:cancel_branch, _}/:cancel_join outcome is pure, in-memory-only, and no caller persists it today -- so there is no second exercised persistence path for it to diverge from; the AC's 'compared explicitly' requirement is satisfiable by TEST-DESIGNER against the single reachable path. Building the scoped join_counters reconstruction now would add real complexity for a code path that would always take the 'no cohort tracked' no-op branch given the same undisputed persistence gap req048's own MAJOR OQ-3 already disclosed -- REQ-053 (event-replay reconstruction) and REQ-054 (snapshots) are already pending, named requirements in docs/requirements.yaml expected to close this gap; no separate docs/issues/ entry is needed since it is already tracked there and in OQ-2/OQ-3 rather than silently dropped. No anti-patterns.md entries apply to this diff.
